changes.before: A country is emerging from an authoritarian racial system into democratic government after decades of state repression, political killings, torture, disappearances and violence by state and non-state actors. The transition was negotiated rather than produced by total military defeat. Evidence is incomplete and many perpetrators retain knowledge that may never become public through ordinary prosecution. Victims want truth, accountability and repair, while the new democracy must reduce recurrence and avoid renewed political violence. A proposed commission would receive public victim testimony, investigate gross violations, recommend reparations and allow individuals to apply for amnesty for politically motivated acts only if they make full disclosure.
changes.after: A country is emerging from an authoritarian racial system into democratic government after decades of state repression, political killings, torture, disappearances and violence by state and non-state actors. The transition was negotiated rather than produced by total military defeat. Evidence is incomplete. The claim that amnesty will elicit information unavailable through ordinary prosecution is an incentive hypothesis whose size and necessity are uncertain. Victims want truth, accountability and repair, while the new democracy must reduce recurrence and avoid renewed political violence. The commission design under review would investigate gross violations, receive testimony, recommend reparations and consider individual applications for amnesty for qualifying politically associated acts on full disclosure. It would also extinguish the applicant’s criminal and civil liability and specified state, organisational and vicarious civil liabilities; civil remedies can therefore be lost even against nonapplicants. The design provides recommendation, regulation and funding processes for reparation, without establishing that adequate payments or rehabilitation services are secured. Victim choice over all testimony is a proposed additional safeguard; the historical design permits compelled evidence and ordinarily public hearings with protective exceptions.
